decisions.reason: As a close extension of the firm's core pipeline and fittings business, it likely meets aspiration levels more easily and uses existing capabilities and customer relationships, so management would tend to retain it.

Although the firm can manufacture and coat it, a public waste bin is distant from its core infrastructure offer and likely to fall short of aspiration relative to core products, making reallocation of resources plausible.
This waste bin variant is also distant from the established business and adds complexity in a non-core line, so boundedly rational management would likely discontinue it if results are only mediocre.

Outdoor public ashtrays are the most peripheral to the firm's main product-market focus, so they are the most likely to be judged below aspiration and dropped in favor of core or better-fitting developments.
